title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
source_used: ScienceDaily, carrying a release from the Indian Institute of Science (IISc)
key_facts: IISc researchers combined machine learning with quantum-mechanics simulations to identify 9,389 individual reactions on a copper catalyst for turning carbon dioxide into fuels, growing a network of 152 hand-simulated reactions.
They trained ML models to estimate energy barriers and examined reactions among 105 chemical species on the catalyst surface.

The 152-reaction network wrongly predicted formic acid, not methanol, as the main product and underestimated CO2 conversion; the 9,389-reaction network correctly identified methanol and carbon monoxide and raised predicted CO2 conversion about 40 times.
The larger network revealed hydrogen can transfer to intermediates as intact H2, challenging a long-standing assumption.
Published in Nature Communications; experiments were done at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's Green R&D Centre and at A*STAR in Singapore.
The approach could be used for other processes such as nitrogen reduction and water splitting.
quote_evidence: When we modeled the process using the 152 reactions considered initially, the network wrongly predicted formic acid, not methanol, as the major product, and underestimated how much CO2 gets converted.
Materials provided by Indian Institute of Science (IISc).
why_it_matters_hint: A bigger, machine-learning-built reaction map matched experiments and pointed to a hydrogen route that could guide catalyst design.
event_date: Release dated 13 Oct 2026 (ScienceDaily URL); Nature Communications publication date not stated
